findings.title: Fixed Event Battles and the automatic Arverni Phase omit Battle capability hooks
findings.expected: Every enemy Battle Command, including free Event Battles and automatic Arverni Ambushes, applies Balearic Slingers once. A holder of shaded Germanic Horse doubles the enemy Losses in a selected eligible Region of its Event-granted Battle. The printed Event exceptions remain intact.
findings.observed: With Card13 active, public numeric2 shaded at Carnutes resolves four Aedui Warbands versus two Roman Auxilia into four Aedui/no Auxilia, with no Slingers request. No Legions are present, so card2 adds no live combat modifier; the matched ordinary Battle asks Slingers and leaves three Aedui/one Auxilia. Card25 and36 likewise ignore third-party Roman Slingers. Card36 with shaded Horse owned by its Aedui executor leaves six of eight Belgic Warbands instead of four, and never asks Horse. Full run_arverni_phase in an At War Carnutes position adds its legal Ally during Rally, skips March on Frost and cannot Raid zero Roman Resources, then Ambushes without Slingers: four Arverni/no Auxilia survive instead of three Arverni/one Auxilia.
findings.cause: _resolve_fixed_event_battle and _arverni_phase_battle call resolve_battle directly; neither supplies the Command-level Slingers/Horse choice and execution hooks installed in _execute_battle. The capability calculations depend on that orchestration. All confirmed symptoms are grouped as one remaining alternate-path integration defect.

For the unshaded Capability, any Ambush is a Battle Command (3.3.4, 5.4). Romans could have Auxilia cause Losses to an attacker Battling another Faction in the Region.
If Gallic, take this card. Each Battle Command, you double enemy’s Losses in 1 Region unless Defender with Fort/Citadel.

Free Battle in either Pictones or Arverni Region, inflicting 3 extra Losses, 1 Ally (not Citadel) first.

Battle with Ambush (3.3.4, 3.4.4, 4.1) in each Region where the Arverni currently are able to do so ... and would cause an enemy Loss.
When executing Event text, follow normal rules, such as restrictions and procedures for free actions granted (5.4), unless otherwise specified.

findings.title: Stalwart fails to cancel Ballistae protection of Roman Forts
findings.expected: After shaded A31 is acquired, earlier Ballistae unshaded cannot protect a Roman Fort from German Battle Losses. A Fort absorbing a Loss on die roll3 must be removed under the ordinary 1–3 rule.
findings.observed: Four German Warbands attacking a lone Roman Fort in Carnutes generate one Loss after halving. At seed7 the next and only RNG roll is3. Ballistae+Stalwart leaves the Fort standing; Ballistae without Stalwart does the same. With Stalwart but no Ballistae the Fort is removed. A matched non-German Belgic attacker correctly leaves the Ballistae-protected Fort standing.
findings.cause: resolve_losses changes every FORT absorption threshold to2 whenever unshaded Ballistae is active. It has no inflicting-faction context and does not apply shaded A31 cancellation. The recent A31 repairs reached named-leader rates, LegioX and Slingers, but not this casualty consumer.

If two Events contradict, the currently played Event takes precedence.

findings.title: Shaded Surus permits multiple base-game German March groups from one origin
findings.expected: Shaded Surus grants March, Raid or Battle using its newly placed German Warbands. Base Germanic March may form at most one moving group per origin; a subset may stay. A split into two moving groups must be rejected before any replacements or moves commit.
findings.observed: The public shaded Surus Event replaces four Aedui Warbands at Treveri, then accepts a two-Warband group to Nervii plus a two-Warband extra group to Sequani. Both destinations gain German Control. The same forbidden split succeeds via explicit_moves, a production terminal-collected plan, and a durable pending/save/load/resume response that replays exactly. All pre/post schema and structural checks pass.
findings.cause: Surus routes its base-game German Command through the generic free-action validator/executor. The shared validator counts distinct selected origins, and _collect_march_moves appends extra_groups or returns explicit_moves without enforcing the original-game German one-moving-group rule. The terminal also offers further groups without a base-German gate.

source_refs.quote: The Germanic Tribes Faction during the Germans Phase (6.2) or when guided by another Faction via Enlist (4.5.1) or Event (5.0) uses Commands similar to those of the Gauls (3.3), but costing 0 and differing as follows.
Germanic Warbands within a March origin Region may form at most a single moving Group to enter one adjacent Region (any Warbands may stay behind).
In a Region within 1 of Treveri, replace up to 4 Aedui Warbands with German March, Raid, or Battle with them.

findings.controls: On the identical source board, a single group of all four moves legally to Nervii. A single two-Warband group moves to Nervii while two remain legally at Treveri. The tested split representations instead create two separate moving groups. No resident Germans, Leaders, Harassment or timing actions complicate the witness.

None reports this original-game Surus group-count validation gap; this does not reopen those closed findings.

findings.title: Non-Roman non-player Quarters never execute their evacuation or Leader-consolidation procedures
findings.expected: Non-player Belgae, Aedui, and base-game Arverni evacuate eligible Devastated Regions when a legal refuge exists; expansion Germans likewise evacuate when lacking an Ally or Settlement. Belgae, Arverni, and Germans also consolidate their Leader with the largest reachable Warband group under their printed priorities and leave-behind restrictions.
findings.observed: Public quarters_phase returns empty non-Roman relocation lists in every NPC case. Each evacuation witness leaves three Warbands at Devastated Carnutes and rolls [2,5,1], removing two, although the legal matched move puts all three into their own non-Devastated Bituriges (four Warbands there, zero losses). Leader cases leave each Leader with three Warbands when a legal relocation can join ten. An actual Pax Gallica setup first Winter reproduces the Aedui omission through run_winter_round: the Germans Phase is properly skipped, Aedui lose two Carnutes Warbands on [2,5,2], and the explicit-relocation control preserves all four.
findings.cause: winter._quarters_phase invokes build_np_winter_relocations only for Romans; every other NPC receives {faction: []}. Existing node_b_quarters/node_a_quarters/node_v_quarters/node_g_quarters are referenced only by definitions and tests, and their legacy descriptive payloads do not match the executable relocation tuple schema.
